This whole bill is an
example of bureaucracy in full force and power, bureaucracy being most careful to stretch as much red tape as it possibly can around all exchange regulations and transactions. The persons who drew up this bill, as far as I can see, were so insistent on stopping up all holes through which any capital might get out of the country that they have carried it to the extent of stopping up a lot which exists purely in their own minds; and this clause is an example of it. It prevents anyone in this country from performing any services for a person in another country. The result of it is that if you have a friend or relative in a foreign country you are not permitted to sell any real estate for him, or to buy real estate, or perform any service of the kind without getting a permit from the board. Of course quite a number of services of this kind people frequently wish to perform without any remuneration; but in any case under this section you must not receive remuneration for a service.
When the matter was being discussed in the committee I asked an expert witness if there was any real reason or necessity for this clause, and the only answer I could get from him was that it was put there in order to prevent a resident of Canada from building up a credit abroad. That is no reason at all. Under another section of the act, any credit which any resident of this country builds up or secures abroad, through a sale of goods or in any other way, the board can force him to bring back to Canada. In view of the fact that the board has that power of compelling the Canadian resident to bring into Canada any securities or credits he may have in a foreign country, I can see no necessity for this clause. It is just a piece of useless red tape which further complicates the matter and makes it a nuisance. Therefore I move that the bill be amended by deleting clause 32.

speechtext:
Before the orders of the day are called I should like to address a question to the Minister of Trans-
IMr. Abbott.]
port. Has a report been received about the removal of the wrecked SS. Beaverhill from Hillyard's reef where it went aground on November 24, 1944, and if so, can the minister tell us when the wreck will be removed?

speakerposition: Minister of Transport
maintopic: SS. "BEAVERHILL" QUESTION AS TO REMOVAL OF WRECK FROM SAINT JOHN HARBOUR
speechtext: The hon. gentleman telephoned my office a short while before I came down to the house, so I have not a complete report on the subject matter. From memory I can state that the SS. Beaverhill has been in the harbour of Saint John for almost two years. This vessel was owned by the Canadian Pacific Railway Company, and it was abandoned by that company to the insurance company which in turn entered into a contract with Foundation Maritimes Limited to remove it at a very high cost. The position to-day, I am informed, is that the contractor is awaiting favourable tidal conditions in order to remove it, possibly at the end of this month. The department officials are doing everything they can to expedite its removal. I am further informed that it is not interfering with traffic.

speechtext: Mr. Speaker, I should like to address a question to the Minister of Transport, a copy of which has been delivered to him. speakerposition: Minister of Transport

speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, the department
officials have given consideration to the placing of one or other of the Scotias on the strait of Northumberland during exhibition or old home week in Charlottetown, but the position with reference to the two Scotias is this. Scotia I is now in dry dock at Halifax, and will not be out for some two or three weeks. As soon as it is released, Scotia II, which is in need of extensive repairs, will have to go into dry dock and will not be released until the month of November. During the month of November the weather is so rough in the strait of Northumberland that the department officials think it would be dangerous to add either Scotia I or II to the present Prince Edward Island car ferry service. But in order to relieve the congestion that might arise during old home week it is proposed that the Prince Edward Island car ferry be used to its maximum

maintopic: P.E.I. CAR FERRY SERVICE USE OF "SCOTIA" FOR OLD HOME WEEK- SS. "ABEG'WEIT"
speechtext: My hon. friend knows that the foreign exchange control board will not allow a Canadian who goes to the United States to export his Canadian capital to that country unless a permit is granted.

maintopic: P.E.I. CAR FERRY SERVICE USE OF "SCOTIA" FOR OLD HOME WEEK- SS. "ABEG'WEIT"
speechtext: I know of all the prohibitions of the board, but what I want the committee to understand is why? Why are there to be prohibitions against that which in no way interferes with what the board would1 otherwise have?

maintopic: P.E.I. CAR FERRY SERVICE USE OF "SCOTIA" FOR OLD HOME WEEK- SS. "ABEG'WEIT"
speechtext: Tory filibuster.

maintopic: P.E.I. CAR FERRY SERVICE USE OF "SCOTIA" FOR OLD HOME WEEK- SS. "ABEG'WEIT"
speechtext: Because of the prescience of the individual in looking after his old age he has provided himself with funds at no cost to the board. He has in no way interfered with the board. speakerposition: Minister of National Defence; Minister of National Defence for Naval Services
